title: Kinetic Predicted-Moment Flux Reconstruction for High-Order High-Performance Fluid Simulation
abstract: KPM-FR is a spatially high-order kinetic-based scheme for low-Mach-number weakly compressible flows that simultaneously advances high fidelity, large throughput, and minimal memory footprint. Rooted in the gas-kinetic scheme (GKS), it derives numerical fluxes from the locally evolved Boltzmann-BGK equation to recover Navier-Stokes solutions, but carries out kinetic evolution entirely in moment space within a high-order flux reconstruction (FR) framework via a concise predictor-corrector scheme. This maps to two fused GPU kernels per time step, confining intermediate data to on-chip memory. It reduces per-point memory more than fivefold vs LBM, exhibits lower numerical dissipation than cumulant LBM, and sustains over 8 billion solution-point updates/sec on a single RTX 4090 at only 42 bytes/point, scaling to 1.8 billion solution points on a single workstation.
nature: Novel architecture + System design + Heavy math derivation
